about: Concept graph of the Python track: what each concept needs first (requires), what it lets you do (can), and where it is taught (lesson) and practised (exercises). Shared and learner-free; the learner's own evidence lives in progress/graph.json. Format: docs/TRACKS.md, 'Concept graph'.

concepts.name: Values, types and expressions
concepts.can: Can predict the value and type of an expression mixing int, float, str and bool (7 // 2, 7 / 2, '3' * 2, 3 > 2 and 'a')

concepts.name: Conditions
concepts.can: Can predict which branch of an if / elif / else chain runs, including the order of the tests

concepts.name: Lists and indexing
concepts.can: Can say what xs[0], xs[-1] and len(xs) give, and which index raises IndexError

concepts.name: for loops
concepts.can: Can trace a for loop over a list and write down the loop variable on each pass

concepts.name: range
concepts.can: Can list the numbers range(a, b, step) produces, including negative steps and the excluded end

concepts.name: Functions and return
concepts.can: Can tell what a function returns on every path, including the None returned by a missing return

concepts.name: Accumulators
concepts.can: Can choose the start value of an accumulator and say where in the loop it is updated and where it is returned

concepts.name: Best so far
concepts.can: Can keep the best value seen so far and pick a safe start value (the first item, not 0)

concepts.name: enumerate
concepts.can: Can loop over index and value together and return the first index where a condition holds

concepts.name: Floats and rounding
concepts.can: Can explain why 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 and keep money exact by working in integer cents

concepts.name: Slicing
concepts.can: Can write down xs[a:b:c] for any a, b, c, including negative values and out-of-range ends

concepts.name: split and join
concepts.can: Can predict s.split() against s.split(' ') on repeated spaces, and rebuild a string with ' '.join

concepts.name: Cleaning strings
concepts.can: Can normalise text (lower, strip, keep only letters) before comparing it

concepts.name: zip
concepts.can: Can pair neighbours with zip(xs, xs[1:]) and say how many pairs a list of n items gives

concepts.name: Comprehensions
concepts.can: Can turn a filter-and-transform loop into a comprehension and back, keeping the order of for and if

concepts.name: Runs
concepts.can: Can group equal neighbours into runs and remember to close the last run after the loop

concepts.name: match with list patterns
concepts.can: Can predict which case of a match on a list of words runs, including captures and the * rest pattern

concepts.name: Dictionaries
concepts.can: Can predict d[k], d.get(k, default), k in d and looping over d.items()

concepts.name: Counting with a dict
concepts.can: Can predict the result of a loop that does d[k] = d.get(k, 0) + 1 over a list

concepts.name: Grouping
concepts.can: Can build a dict of lists keyed by a derived value (setdefault or a membership test) and say what each list holds

concepts.name: Sets
concepts.can: Can say what a set keeps (unique items, no order) and that membership is about one step

concepts.name: Seen-sets
concepts.can: Can find the first repeat in one pass with a set of items already seen

concepts.name: Set operations
concepts.can: Can pick &, |, - or ^ for a question about two collections and say what order the result has

concepts.name: Text to records
concepts.can: Can split lines of text into fields and turn them into tuples or dicts, skipping blank lines

concepts.name: Parse, then act
concepts.can: Can separate parsing a line from deciding what to do with it, so each part can be tested alone

concepts.name: Config files
concepts.can: Can parse key = value lines with comments and stray spaces into a dict

concepts.name: CSV
concepts.can: Can read a header row and turn each following row into a dict keyed by the header

concepts.name: Logs: parse, group, aggregate
concepts.can: Can turn log lines into counts or per-key summaries, then sort or filter them

concepts.name: Scanning characters
concepts.can: Can walk a string character by character, building a number until a unit letter closes it

concepts.name: Regular expressions basics
concepts.can: Can read a simple pattern with groups and say what re.findall returns for it

concepts.name: lambda
concepts.can: Can rewrite a one-line function as a lambda and say when a def is clearer

concepts.name: Sort keys
concepts.can: Can sort by several fields with a key returning a tuple, including one field in reverse

concepts.name: try / except
concepts.can: Can predict which except block catches an error and what runs after it

concepts.name: Raising errors
concepts.can: Can choose ValueError or TypeError for bad input and raise it with a useful message

concepts.name: Default and keyword arguments
concepts.can: Can predict which parameter gets which value in a call mixing positional, keyword and default arguments

concepts.name: *args and **kwargs
concepts.can: Can say what args and kwargs hold inside a function for a given call

concepts.name: Type hints and docstrings
concepts.can: Can read and write a signature such as def f(xs: list[int], n: int = 3) -> dict[str, int]

concepts.name: Higher-order functions
concepts.can: Can pass a function as an argument, call it inside, and say when it runs

concepts.name: Closures
concepts.can: Can predict what an inner function remembers from its enclosing call, and when nonlocal is needed

concepts.name: Classes and state
concepts.can: Can write a class whose methods read and change self attributes and predict its state after a few calls

concepts.name: Properties
concepts.can: Can use @property for a computed or validated attribute and say when the setter runs

concepts.name: Class attributes
concepts.can: Can predict when an attribute is shared by every instance and when assigning creates an instance copy

concepts.name: Custom exceptions
concepts.can: Can define an exception class and catch it separately from built-in errors

concepts.name: Dunder methods
concepts.can: Can say which dunder method print, ==, + and len call on an object

concepts.name: Dataclasses
concepts.can: Can say which methods @dataclass writes for you and why a mutable default needs field(default_factory=...)

concepts.name: Inheritance and composition
concepts.can: Can predict which method an overridden call runs, and choose 'has a' over 'is a' when it fits

concepts.name: Using the debugger
concepts.can: Can set a breakpoint, step over and into lines, and watch a variable change

concepts.name: Classic logic bugs
concepts.can: Can spot a wrong start value, an early return inside a loop and an off-by-one by tracing a small input

concepts.name: Changing a list while looping over it
concepts.can: Can explain why removing items from a list inside a for loop over it skips items, and fix it with a new list

concepts.name: Sets do not keep order
concepts.can: Can remove duplicates while keeping the first-seen order

concepts.name: Theory: names, objects and memory
concepts.can: Can draw names as arrows to objects and say which objects are mutable

concepts.name: Names vs objects
concepts.can: Can predict the result of a = b followed by a change through one name, for a list and for an int

concepts.name: Mutability
concepts.can: Can explain why a mutable default argument keeps its changes between calls

concepts.name: Aliasing
concepts.can: Can predict the grid after [[0] * 3] * 3 and one assignment, and build it without aliasing

concepts.name: Shallow and deep copies
concepts.can: Can say which changes a shallow copy shares with the original and when deepcopy is needed

concepts.name: Scope
concepts.can: Can predict when assigning inside a function makes a new local name, and what global and nonlocal change

concepts.name: Late binding
concepts.can: Can predict what lambdas made in a loop return, and fix it with a default argument

concepts.name: Theory: the call stack
concepts.can: Can draw the frames of nested calls and say in which order they return

concepts.name: Generators
concepts.can: Can predict which values a generator yields and when its body runs (only when asked for the next value)

concepts.name: Decorators
concepts.can: Can say what @deco above def f does in plain assignments, and write a wrapper that passes its arguments on

concepts.name: Context managers
concepts.can: Can say when __enter__ and __exit__ run, including when the block raises

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.can: Can name the base case and the smaller problem, and trace a recursive call on a small input

concepts.name: Tracing by hand
concepts.can: Can fill in a table of variable values, line by line, for unfamiliar code

concepts.name: Predicting output
concepts.can: Can predict the exact printed output of code that mixes references, built-ins and loops

concepts.name: Reading and writing files
concepts.can: Can read a text file line by line with a with block, and say what happens to the trailing newline

concepts.name: pathlib
concepts.can: Can build paths with / and list files with glob without string joining

concepts.name: json
concepts.can: Can save and load a dict with json, and say which Python types do not survive the round trip

concepts.name: datetime
concepts.can: Can parse a date, subtract two dates and read the days from the timedelta

concepts.name: collections
concepts.can: Can replace a counting loop with Counter and a grouping loop with defaultdict(list)

concepts.name: random and testable randomness
concepts.can: Can pass a seeded random.Random into a function so its result can be tested

concepts.name: Modules and __main__
concepts.can: Can split code into a module, import it, and say when the if __name__ == '__main__' block runs

concepts.name: Command-line arguments
concepts.can: Can define positional and optional arguments with argparse and read them back

concepts.name: Writing tests with pytest
concepts.can: Can write parametrised pytest tests, including one that expects an error

concepts.name: Theory: Big-O
concepts.can: Can count the steps of a loop and of a nested loop as the input grows and name the Big-O

concepts.name: Theory: space complexity
concepts.can: Can say how much extra memory a solution uses as the input grows, separately from its time

concepts.name: Hash maps and sets for speed
concepts.can: Can replace a nested search with a dict or set lookup (the complement trick) and state the new Big-O

concepts.name: Using sorted order
concepts.can: Can say what sorting first buys (order to move by) and what it costs (O(n log n))

concepts.name: Two pointers
concepts.can: Can move a left and a right index towards each other on a sorted list and say why no pair is missed

concepts.name: In-place changes
concepts.can: Can change a list in place with a write index, using O(1) extra space

concepts.name: Palindromes with two pointers
concepts.can: Can check a palindrome from both ends, skipping characters that do not count

concepts.name: Fixed sliding window
concepts.can: Can slide a window of size k, adding the item that enters and removing the one that leaves

concepts.name: Variable sliding window
concepts.can: Can grow a window on the right and shrink it on the left until a condition holds again

concepts.name: Theory: stacks and queues as ADTs
concepts.can: Can say what LIFO and FIFO mean and which operations each type promises, whatever stores it

concepts.name: Stacks
concepts.can: Can use a list as a stack (append, pop) to match brackets or undo steps

concepts.name: Queues
concepts.can: Can process items first in, first out, and say why list.pop(0) makes that slow

concepts.name: collections.deque
concepts.can: Can use deque for O(1) appends and pops at both ends, including a bounded window with maxlen

concepts.name: Monotonic stack
concepts.can: Can find the next greater item for every position in one pass with a stack kept in order

concepts.name: Theory: logarithms and invariants
concepts.can: Can say how many halvings reduce n items to one, and state a loop invariant

concepts.name: Binary search
concepts.can: Can write binary search with correct bounds and say what lo and hi mean at every step
concepts.lesson: on arrays and on the answer

concepts.name: Binary search on the answer
concepts.can: Can binary-search a numeric answer when a yes/no check is monotonic
concepts.lesson: on arrays and on the answer

concepts.name: Backtracking
concepts.can: Can generate subsets and permutations by choosing, recursing and undoing the choice

concepts.name: Merge sort
concepts.can: Can split, sort each half recursively and merge, and explain O(n log n)

concepts.name: Linked lists
concepts.can: Can reverse a linked list by moving next pointers, drawing each step

concepts.name: Fast and slow pointers
concepts.can: Can find the middle of a linked list or detect a cycle with two pointers at different speeds

concepts.name: Binary trees
concepts.can: Can traverse a tree in pre-, in- and post-order and compute its depth recursively

concepts.name: Level-order traversal
concepts.can: Can visit a tree level by level with a queue

concepts.name: Binary search trees
concepts.can: Can search and insert in a BST and say why an in-order walk is sorted

concepts.name: Graphs: BFS
concepts.can: Can find the shortest path in steps on a grid or adjacency list with BFS and a seen-set

concepts.name: Graphs: DFS
concepts.can: Can count connected regions with DFS, recursive or with a stack

concepts.name: Topological sort
concepts.can: Can order tasks with dependencies using in-degrees and a queue, and detect a cycle

concepts.name: Heaps
concepts.can: Can keep the top k items with heapq and say why it beats sorting everything

concepts.name: Intervals and greedy choices
concepts.can: Can merge overlapping intervals after sorting by start, and argue why a greedy choice is safe

concepts.name: Dynamic programming
concepts.can: Can define a subproblem, write its recurrence and memoise it, then turn it into a table

concepts.name: Small design: LRU and TTL caches
concepts.can: Can design an LRU cache with O(1) get and put and explain the data structures chosen
